abstract: The exact risk of developing a second primary cancer following radiotherapy for testicular seminoma is not known. At the Northern Israel Oncology Center, between the years 1968-1988, 75 patients with early stage (I,IIA) testicular seminoma were treated by orchiectomy followed by radiation therapy. The overall 10- and 20-year survival probability was 95% and 90%, respectively. Eight patients (11%) developed nine second cancers, with a cumulative rate of one case per 1,000 years of follow-up. The second primary cancers were: two bronchogenic carcinomas, one contralateral seminoma, one thymoma, one papillary carcinoma of the thyroid, one carcinoma of the stomach, one transitional cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder, one carcinoma of the colon, and one malignant melanoma. Three of these tumors developed within the irradiated field. Five of these eight patients are alive with no evidence of recurrent cancer. We conclude that patients treated for seminoma have an increased risk of developing a second cancer. There is a need for greater awareness of this possibility. The overall prognosis remains favorable.
abstract_ja: 早期病期(病期I・IIA)の精巣セミノーマ患者75例について、精巣摘除術後に放射線療法を施行された1968年から1988年の症例を検討した。10年および20年生存率は、それぞれ95%および90%であった。8例(11%)に計9個の二次癌が発生し、累積発生率は1,000年の追跡あたり1例であった。そのうち3腫瘍は照射野内に発生した。セミノーマ治療後の患者は二次癌の発生リスクが高く、その可能性への認識を高める必要がある。それでも全体の予後は良好である。
